requirements.evidence: app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:36-42 locks the queue row and rejects an inactive queue using the database state; :45-52 and :113-126 implement any/priority_only/normal_only with priority desc, issued_at asc, id asc; :54-75 lock each candidate, re-check it is still waiting, and save only status/called_at/called_by_user_id before returning it; :83-108 implements the 3-call fairness rule by called_at desc then id desc. The contract is present: app/Enums/CallMode.php:6-9 (any/priority_only/normal_only) and app/Exceptions/NoWaitingTicketsException.php:7 (extends RuntimeException), reusing InactiveQueueException; docs were updated at docs/business-rules.md:133-144 and docs/architecture.md:110-138.

conventions.evidence: The domain write lives in app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php as an invokable action, matching the project's action convention; the enum is in app/Enums and the exception in app/Exceptions. Docs are kept in sync (docs/business-rules.md:133-144, docs/architecture.md:110-138) and CHANGELOG.md:21 records the change. Tests are Pest with RefreshDatabase (tests/Feature/CallNextTicketTest.php:15). No service/repository layer or new dependency was introduced, and no authorization was added because task.md:11-12 explicitly excludes it.

security.evidence: There is no untrusted input surface: the mode is a typed CallMode enum (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:28-32) and the queue/user come from models, with lookups using whereKey. The winner is updated attribute-by-attribute (:67-70), not through mass assignment, so $fillable/$guarded cannot be abused. No authorization is required by the task (trusted caller), and there is no Blade/HTML output or secret handling in the change.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/CallNextTicketTest.php covers priority/age/id ordering (:34-82), queue scoping and already-called tickets (:84-107), persistence and return value (:109-127), each call mode (:129-152), the fairness rule including id tie-break, other queues, priority_only history and normal reset (:154-302), inactive and stale queue instances (:304-327), no-candidate and empty queues (:329-348), and the concurrent-call skip path via a retrieved hook (:350-373). These are meaningful assertions on selected tickets and persisted state, not weakened or skipped tests.

simplicity.evidence: A single 127-line action with three small private helpers (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:83-126) reuses the existing Ticket model, TicketStatus enum, InactiveQueueException and DB::transaction. The candidate filters and fairness check are each expressed once; there is no speculative abstraction, duplication or added package.

readability.evidence: Names are explicit (`mustProtectNormalTickets`, `candidatesQuery`, `$restrictToNormal`), public behavior is documented with PHPDoc and @throws (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:18-27), and non-obvious decisions are commented (:34-35, :54-56, :79-82). The test cases are named after the rule they verify, and there is no dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: The diff only adds the required action (app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php), enum (app/Enums/CallMode.php), exception (app/Exceptions/NoWaitingTicketsException.php) and its Pest test, plus the required docs (docs/business-rules.md, docs/architecture.md) and the conventional CHANGELOG entry. It contains no HTTP/Livewire, authorization, recall/skip or unrelated refactors.

review.summary: The change implements App\Actions\CallNextTicket with the required CallMode enum and NoWaitingTicketsException, reading and locking the queue row, rejecting inactive queues, applying deterministic ordering and the 3-call fairness rule, and ensuring exactly-once selection by locking each candidate and re-checking its status. The behaviour is covered by thorough Pest tests, including fairness edge cases, stale queue state and a concurrent-call skip, and the required business-rules and architecture docs are updated. No material issues were found; approve as is.
